definition: Checking booked trades for the right counterparty, terms, classification and cross-system links, and rebooking or correcting deals that are wrong.

synthesis.description: A round starts when someone in risk, credit, settlements or the trading desk spots a deal booked wrong: the wrong counterparty, a missing EOL or Sitara link, a physical deal not marked for its financial component, or double entry. Darron Giron or Bill Williams asks the booker to change the counterparty in Tagg, update the link fields or rebook the deal, and confirms once the deal looks right in both Tagg and Sitara. Some rounds become a larger reconciliation against another party's records before deals can be valued.
steps: Someone notices a booking problem, from credit, a DPR or SAR run, or a counterparty query.
The deal is looked up in Tagg, Sitara or Enpower and compared with what was traded.
The correct counterparty short name, deal type or link number is identified.
The booker is asked to rebook, relink or change the counterparty.
The deal is changed, or zeroed out and re-entered when it was a duplicate.
The requester checks both systems and confirms the deal is booked correctly.
synthesis.approach: A nightly exception report comparing Tagg, Sitara and Enpower could flag deals with missing EOL or Sitara links, counterparty names that do not match the credit-approved short name, physical deals without the financial flag, and duplicate entries in the same book, so bookers receive a list of specific fixes instead of one-off emails.
synthesis.rationale: Most rounds are the same few checks (counterparty short name, link fields, deal classification, duplicates). A booking checklist used at entry time would catch them before credit or settlements does, and is something the desk can adopt immediately before any report is built.
